{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for pastries|servings=10|time=6–10 hours|difficulty=4|image=[[File:Jachnun.jpg|300px|Jahnun]]
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Jachnun''' is a Yemenite [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastry]] made of worked dough (made without the use of [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]])<ref>{{Citation |contribution=The Yemenite Cuisine |title=Ascending the Palm Tree: An Anthology of the Yemenite Jewish Heritage|last1=Mizrachi|first1=Avshalom|author-link1= |editor1=Rachel Yedid|editor2=Danny Bar-Maoz|publisher=E'ele BeTamar|place=Rehovot|page=134 |year=2018 |language=en |oclc=1041776317 }}</ref> and traditionally eaten hot during the Sabbath morning meal, after being left to bake all throughout the night within a sealed pot in an oven.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] white [[cookbook:flour|wheat flour]] 
* 10 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] (optional)
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]] (or to taste)
* 1 leveled [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] salt
* 2¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] of water
* [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|Canola oil]]
* 200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]], [[cookbook:margarine|soft margarine]], or shortening
* 10 [[Cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard-boiled eggs]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. Make a well in the center.
# Add some of the water to the well, and mix with your hands. Gradually [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] in the rest of the water, then continue kneading for 15 minutes. The [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] should not be too soft or sticky.
# Tear off a piece of dough the size of your fist. Flatten and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll]] it out on your work surface, then shape again into a ball. Repeat this step for the rest of the dough, then [[Cookbook:Brushing|brush]] all the balls with a thin coating of oil.
# Allow the dough to rest for about 1–2 hours, until they have sunken slightly.
# Roll and stretch each ball out on a greased surface until it is very thin. Try to make the dough as thin as possible without it tearing.
# Spread some soft butter over the whole surface of the flattened dough. Make a triangular fold lengthwise, like a shirt fold: fold one-third of the dough toward the middle then fold the other side. Make a small fold up and down, and start rolling (with greased hands) from the bottom to the top, like folding a sleeping bag. You should be left with an elongated, slightly fat rolled ''jachnun''. Repeat this shaping step for all the dough balls.
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{convert|212|F}}. Line a pot with slices of bread or [[Cookbook:Pita|pita]] so that it does not become overly dry while baking in the oven.
# Place the unbaked ''jachnun'' into a cookie bag, with each bag holding a single layer of ''jachnun''. This prevents loss of moisture. Stack the ''jachnun'' in the pot, with 2–3 rows stacked one on top of the other in a criss-crossed fashion (horizontally and vertically).
# Cover the pot with the lid, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in the preheated oven for 6–10 hours.
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard-boiled eggs]] and [[Cookbook:Salsa|tomato salsa]], with a little [[Cookbook:Zhug|zhug]] over the paste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The dough cooks best when left to refrigerate for one day prior to baking.
* Since hard-boiled eggs are served with the ''jachnun'', they can be simultaneously cooked in a separate pot of water within the same heated oven.
